validation.summary: Of 350 synthetic movers hidden in NEOWISE-like skies with the real NEOWISE cadence, the search found 99% of those with W1−W2 = 0 moving at least 1″/yr with W2 ≤ 13 (100% at W2 = 14.5, 96% at W2 = 15.5, 100% of bright ones moving only 0.2″/yr), measured their motion to 0.1% (median), and reported 0.00 false movers per survey tile on mover-free skies. For redder objects (W1−W2 = 2, like cold brown dwarfs) it found 97% at W2 ≤ 14.5 and 0% at W2 = 15.5. On real NEOWISE data it recovered 8 of 9 known fast-moving stars (Kapteyn's Star, WISE 0855-0714, Barnard's Star, Luhman 16, Wolf 359, Lalande 21185, Proxima Centauri, Epsilon Indi B).
validation.method: Injection-recovery: we build synthetic NEOWISE single-exposure detection tables that copy the real NEOWISE observing pattern (exposure times, scan ids and frames of real data, about 21 visits from 2014 to 2024), fill them with field stars, galaxies, passing asteroids and spurious detections, hide movers of known speed, direction and brightness in them, and run the survey's mover search without telling it where they are. Noise, detection limits and positional errors follow a model measured on real NEOWISE detections. A hidden mover counts as recovered when the search reports a mover within 5″ of it with a motion within 30% (or 0.1″/yr). False positives are counted on skies with no movers at all, and the search is also run on real NEOWISE data around stars whose motion Gaia DR3 measured.
limits: Synthetic skies use high-Galactic-latitude source counts; crowded fields near the Galactic plane are not simulated at their full density.
Every exposure covers the whole synthetic patch; real frame edges and gaps are only present when injecting into real tables.
The noise model is calibrated on two real 4′ NEOWISE fields; it has no blending, no position-dependent systematics and a simple saturation model.
Injected movers have parallaxes from a tangential velocity of 80 km/s and do not accelerate (no binaries).
False-positive rates are measured on synthetic skies; real artefacts (latents, ghosts, scattered light) are more varied.
Known-star checks use small 4′ cut-outs of real data and, when available, the survey's own tile results.

method: Each processed tile holds every NEOWISE single-exposure detection from 2014 to 2024 (about 20 million per tile). Detections that fail basic quality cuts (artefact flags, bad frames, moonlight, weak signal) are dropped. WISE scanned each part of the sky about every six months, so the detections of one source in one scan are averaged into a single position per visit. Those positions are linked across the ten years into tracks, including fast movers of up to 12 arcseconds per year, and a straight-line fit gives each track's proper motion and its uncertainty. Tracks seen in at least 6 visits that move at least 150 mas per year with at least 5 sigma are kept as movers. Each mover is compared with Gaia DR3 stars moved to the same date with their own motion, then ranked: movers that Gaia does not explain, that are red in WISE (a sign of a cold brown dwarf) and that have long, clean tracks come first. The top of the list is for people to investigate.
limits: Only the tiles listed here have been searched; the rest of the sky has not been processed yet.
Motions slower than 150 mas per year or faster than 12 arcseconds per year are not searched.
A source must be detected in at least 6 of the roughly 20 WISE visits, so very faint or very red objects near the detection limit can be missed.

'Unexplained' means no Gaia DR3 star with a matching motion lies within 3 arcseconds. That is expected for cold brown dwarfs too faint for Gaia, but blends, artefacts next to bright stars and tracks cut at tile edges can look the same.
A track that crosses a tile edge can be split in two or appear in both tiles.
Motions come from a straight-line fit; parallax is fitted only where a value is given, so very nearby objects can have slightly biased motions.
A candidate is not a discovery: each one needs a human check of the images and other catalogues first.
The Gaia check is still pending for 288 of 621 tiles with movers (service busy or offline); their movers are 'not checked'.
